Poignant

/POY-nyuhnt/ - the stress falls on POY · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Poignant means deeply affecting, moving.

The most poignant item in the time capsule was a wish list from 1961: every child had asked for something the town could no longer make.

Worked Example

Graduation slideshows earn easy laughs with baby photos, but the poignant slide is always the empty desk kept for the classmate who did not live to graduate — the hall goes quiet a beat before the applause.

Poignant means it pierces: emotion with a sharp point, often bittersweet, true to a root that means 'to prick.' A touching moment warms you; a poignant one leaves a small, exact wound you remember.

How Poignant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

touching

touching: gently moving; poignant cuts sharper and deeper

affecting

affecting: stirs real emotion, without poignant's bittersweet sting

Antonyms

forgettable

forgettable: leaves no mark on the feelings at all

flat

flat: stirs nothing, lands with a thud

How Strong Is It? — touching → poignant → heartrending

touching vs. poignant

touching vs. poignant: Touching is milder than poignant — it warms the heart gently, while poignant pierces it.

heartrending vs. poignant

heartrending vs. poignant: Heartrending goes further than poignant — grief that tears at an audience, rather than a sharp, bittersweet pang.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — poign

Root — poign: to prick, to sting (Latin pungere, via French poindre)

Suffix — -ant

Suffix — -ant: doing, being

Put it together

Put it together: Poign (to prick) + -ant (doing) = pricking, stinging. French cooks still use the same word for a sharp taste; English kept the sharpness and moved it to the heart. A poignant scene is one with a point on it — it doesn't wash over you, it pierces.

Use the root in a new word: puncture

Use the root in a new word: puncture: A stray nail punctured the rear tire, and the long slow hiss ended the road trip.

Word Choice

neutral / literary

Poignant is for moments that pierce — sharp, often bittersweet emotion: a poignant photograph, a poignant pause. 'Touching' warms; poignant stings, true to its prickly root. And when critics want to name the piercing quality itself rather than the moment, they reach for its unit-mate pathos — same territory, more analytical register.
